title: Japanese Lamb Curry with Potatoes (カレーライス風ラムカレー)
ingredients: 5 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
Garnish: sliced green onions & pickled ginger
Option A: 1/2 box (about 100g) Japanese curry roux blocks (Golden Curry, Vermont, etc.)
Option B (homemade roux): 2 tbsp flour, 1 tbsp curry powder, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp ketchup, 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp garam masala
instructions: 1. Sear the lamb: Season lamb cubes generously with salt and pepper. In a Dutch oven or heavy pot, heat 1 tbsp oil over medium-high. Sear lamb cubes until browned on all sides (3–4 min). Remove and set aside.

2. Sauté aromatics & veggies: In the same pot, add sliced onions. Cook until softened and starting to caramelize (6–8 min). Add minced garlic and ginger, cooking for 1 min. Add carrots and potatoes, stirring for 2 min.

3. Add liquids: Return seared lamb to the pot. Pour in 3 cups of broth, honey, mirin, dark soy sauce, and vinegar. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Skim off foam, cover, and cook for 1.5 hours until lamb is fork-tender.

4. Add curry roux: If using store-bought roux: break up curry roux blocks and stir in. Simmer gently for 10–15 min until velvety and glossy. (If using homemade: toast flour and curry powder in 1 tbsp butter for 1 min, whisk in soy sauce, ketchup, Worcestershire, sugar, and 1/2 cup broth, then stir into the main pot.)
5. Serve: Ladle generously over hot steamed Japanese rice. Garnish with chopped green onions and pickled ginger.
notes: Comforting, rich, and mildly sweet. Can also be made in an Instant Pot (high pressure for 35 minutes).
